title: The Arm Still Out
scene: Bus 12 is back on Fourth Ave South at Willis, same rain, same crown in the wheel tracks, same bare maples. Reyna has the reds on and the stop arm is out — bent a few degrees off true from a plow that did not wait. Tobin is already in the street this time, yellow shell, not looking. At the treeline four blocks down, something that heard steel on steel last time has not left. You are behind her again with a clear left lane that is not clear at all. The insulin can wait. He cannot.
decision: Reds are on, the arm is out, and Tobin is in the lane. What do you do?

options.text: Stay stopped behind her until the arm folds and she rolls, even if the left lane is empty
options.result: You sit. Rain on the mesh. Tobin crosses without a glance, then a second kid you did not have last time. The thing at the treeline does not come. Reyna folds the bent arm, finds you in her glass, and does not wave. She does not have to. You are still here. That is the apology.

options.text: Take the left lane now — the arm is already out, so the kids have to be done
options.result: You pull out on reds. Tobin is still in your left headlight. You stand on it. The Menace stops with the plow in the crosswalk he is using. Reyna sees the whole thing in the west-coast glass she does not have. She has a school bus mirror and a bent arm and a face you will carry.

options.text: Creep past the arm on the right shoulder to get out of the thing at the treeline's sightline
options.result: The gravel shoulder puts you around the bent arm and into the space kids use. A backpack scrapes the plating. You are past the bus and still in the rain, and the treeline has you in profile, moving. You did not get quieter. You got closer.

options.text: Tap the horn once so Tobin looks up
options.result: The horn on a stopped bus street. Tobin looks. So does everything else. The treeline starts walking. Reyna's head turns in the glass, not grateful. You made him look and you rang the block doing it.

debrief: Red lamps and an extended stop arm still mean a full stop from both directions until the arm retracts — even when you have been here before, even when the arm is bent because of you. The kid does not check. The street remembers the noise. You do not get to pass it twice.

source.teaching_target: Red lamps and an extended stop arm require a full stop from both directions until the arm retracts; never pass a stopped school bus.

image_brief.subject: Bus 12 stopped in the near lane, red lamps lit, stop arm extended and slightly bent, a dropped backpack on the wet crosswalk paint
image_brief.foreground: wet curb and standing water in the wheel tracks at camera height
image_brief.midground: the Pink Menace stopped behind the bus in the same lane, plow toward the bus, empty-looking left lane beside them
image_brief.background: bare maples, chain-link, flat gray rain, a distant out-of-focus figure at the treeline four blocks down
image_brief.read: reds and the bent arm are on; the backpack is in the lane you wanted last time — no child in frame

geometry.ego_nose_in_frame: the plow blade points toward the bus and the top of the frame
